render.py's job 'refs' dict keys are ref_image SLOT NUMBERS (0..8), and slot N is ALWAYS <Picture N+1> in the prompt text -- slot 0 is <Picture 1> and, on mm_clip_v1, also doubles as GetImageSize's master ref (sets width/height). Authoring a job's refs dict in any order other than the prompt's own <Picture N> order silently swaps identities: a 2026-08-23 apricot_paper proof job put the LOCATION plate in slot 0 (=<Picture 1>, described in the prompt as the character Bram) and every character one slot off -- rendered as a flat character-lineup with no location and no scene, not a crash. Caught by looking at the filmstrip, not by any check. A job's refs dict should be authored by reading off <Picture N> from the prompt line itself, in order, every time.

CONFIRMED (Ronan's call, 2026-08-23): on mm_clip_v1, ref_image_0 is not just 'the master ref that sets size' -- it carries materially more compositional weight than ref_images 1-8. Rule for every multi-reference clip prompt from here: put the LOCATION (or whichever reference should set the scene) at ref_image_0/<Picture 1>, never a character.

Three escalating attempts (0.837 -> 0.638 -> 0.843, non-convergent) is not a sequence where doubling down helps; per LAWS 2 rung 4 this needs a shot-design change (fewer simultaneous character refs, dropping the door-open reveal, or splitting the beat), a call for Ronan not further autonomous rerolling.

b06 attempt 4 (redesigned prompt, gesture instead of door-reveal) measured a genuine ref_leak: correlation UNIFORMLY 0.90-0.904 across all 311 frames (not a spike), confirmed real by comparison against b02 and b03 -- also locked shots at the same gate with characters present, both mean correlation ~0.0-0.03. Matches the vault's own documented WTTB precedent exactly: ref-leak fixed by reroll on an IDENTICAL prompt, seed only (club09j +0.97 -> club09k +0.04). Attempts 1-3 had confounded prompt AND seed changes together; attempt 5 (b06_s130011) reuses attempt 4's prompt verbatim with only the seed changed, to test the documented fix in isolation.

b06 (Bram opens the gate for Reed) attempt 5: seed-only reroll of the redesigned hand-gesture prompt (130010->130011) dropped ref_leak from +0.904 to +0.489, confirming the vault's seed-only-reroll precedent for leak faults specifically. But a second, distinct fault appeared: mean luminance 150.0 vs 97-119 for sibling locked gate shots (b02, b05) -- the model rendered the two gate doors ajar with bright daylight/sky visible through the gap, even though the prompt never asked for the doors to open (retention_analysis only said neither character steps toward the doorway, never stated the doors themselves stay shut).
fix: double-anchored the door state per LAWS §13: added an explicit 'the two iron-banded oak doors stay shut and motionless ... the gap between them never widening and no daylight or yard ever visible through it' clause, stated in both retention_analysis and detailed_description. Requeued as b06_s130012, seed unchanged pattern broken deliberately since this is a genuine prompt-content gap, not a seed-variance issue.

finding: b06 finally passes on attempt 7 (seed 130014). Root cause was two distinct, sequential faults, not one: (1) the door-shut state was never explicitly stated, only implied by 'neither character steps toward the doorway' -- the model rendered the doors ajar with bright daylight beyond, causing mean luminance 150 vs 97-119 for sibling gate shots (fixed by double-anchoring 'doors stay shut ... no daylight ever visible through it' per LAWS 13); (2) once that was fixed, ref_leak stayed pinned 0.7-0.9 across 3 different seeds (130010, 130012, 130013) on a head-on medium-wide composition that centered the arch just as the plate itself does -- not seed noise, since b02/b03's off-center medium shots at the same gate leak near 0.0. Fixed by explicitly describing a three-quarter camera angle favoring Bram's side, breaking the arch's head-on symmetry. Result: ref_leak +0.104, grade 146.4, no blown frames, clipqc passes clean.
fix: Lesson for future beats at a symmetric architectural plate: state camera asymmetry explicitly (favor one side, push the plate's centerline off-frame-center) rather than leaving framing to 'medium-wide' defaults, especially as later beats in a sequence tend to re-anchor 'exactly as the previous beat left them' and drift toward the plate's own centered composition over several beats (b02 leak 0.03 -> b05 0.42 -> b06 0.7-0.9 before the angle fix).

finding: The landed_files integrity bug (landed.py recorded the pre-copy filename, not the actual '<job_id>__'-prefixed name on disk) was silent for the ENTIRE session -- it affected every still-image job too (looks, character/location sheets), not just clip beats, and was only caught because assemble.py happened to be run at the very end of the board. Per founding rule 1 (a check that does not measure the delivered artifact is not a check), this should be caught the moment a job lands, not whenever someone next tries to assemble a cut.
fix: added Contract.check_landed_files() to contract.py: for every unit's jobs.jsonl, every 'landed' row's landed_files entries must exist on disk in clips/ or refs/candidates/. finding: ref_leak reads systematically higher on near-black night scenes than apricot_paper's well-lit ones, even with the subject clearly present and moving (b01/b02 on the forest plate: 4 of 6 attempts REFUSED at 0.53-0.95 despite the witch visibly present in every filmstrip frame). Root cause: at the metric's 64x36 decimation, a small dark-clothed figure against an already near-black, low-variance background contributes almost no differentiating luminance signal versus the empty plate -- unlike apricot_paper's brightly-lit, larger, colourfully-dressed characters. Seed-only reroll (the documented WTTB/apricot_paper fix for genuine leaks) was NOT reliable here -- results swung both ways (0.632->0.951 worse, then ->0.526->0.912 worse again) purely on how much the model happened to render the lantern's light actually washing onto her.
fix: Made the lantern's warm light an explicit, double-anchored instruction (subject_definitions AND retention_analysis AND detailed_description, LAWS 13): 'that flame throws real warm light onto her -- face, hands, cloak -- so she reads as a warm-lit figure, never a flat dark silhouette.' This both improves the shot (matches the intended chiaroscuro look) and gives the correlation metric real differentiating signal. Fixed b02 on the first seed tried after the fix (0.465, down from an untreated 0.5-0.95 range). Standing rule for any dark/night-scene production: describe how the practical light source actually illuminates the subject, don't just describe it as present -- a glowing prop beside a dark figure isn't enough either cinematically or for ref_leak.

finding: A wide, near-static, three-quarter-angle forest shot ('dozens of eyes light the whole width of the forest') failed ref_leak on 4/4 attempts (0.64-0.94) despite fixes for black-frame buildup and 'eyes already lit from frame one'. Unlike the earlier b02/b04-medium confounds, a rigorous full-clip correlation comparison against two ACCEPTED sibling clips (b01 mean 0.375 min 0.216; b04-medium mean 0.372 min 0.132) showed this candidate never dropped below 0.628 for its whole 4.5s duration -- a real structural leak, not a metric artifact, unlike the visually-similar-but-actually-fine cases earlier in this beat sheet.
fix: Cut the beat entirely rather than override the check -- the numeric comparison contradicted the 'looks fine, override it' instinct, so it wasn't overridden even though the user had pre-approved an override in principle. b04's medium framing (a few eyes visible, accepted cleanly at leak 0.468) carries the 'eyes appearing' story beat alone; the full-forest-lit reveal moment was dropped. Standing lesson: 'the witch is visibly present' is necessary but not sufficient to justify overriding ref_leak -- always run the full-clip correlation-vs-accepted-siblings comparison before overriding, exactly as with apricot_paper's b06. A visually convincing shot can still be a real leak.

finding: Ronan's review of both finished boards: shots feel like they 'start over' at every cut. Root cause is structural -- mm_clip_v1 renders every beat independently from the same plates/sheets, tied to its neighbours only by prose ('exactly as the previous shot left them'), which the model cannot honor because it never sees the previous clip's pixels. Prose cannot hold continuity; only pixels can.
fix: Built mm_ifl_v1 (5th frozen graph): MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo pins a clip's first AND last frame to two supplied stills. Proven on last_light's real b01->b02 discontinuity: a 124f bridge rendered between b01's actual last frame and b02's actual first frame measured +0.998 first-frame correlation to the opening still and +0.998 last-frame correlation to the closing still (the two stills themselves correlate only +0.32), with smooth continuous walking motion between. This enables the full storyboard path (routing.md): approve one mm_image still per beat boundary, then render every beat pinned between its two stills -- every cut lands on a literally shared frame, clips render in any order, and the whole film is approved as cheap stills before any clip minute is spent. Also confirms the audio path works through ImageToVideo conditioning (VAEDecodeAudio produced a valid track).

finding: MC character turnaround (puffer jacket + trousers apparel description) sat in a phantom chair in 7 straight attempts across 3 completely different prose strategies -- explicit standing-on-straight-legs language, dropping the feet-height constraint, and a shop-window-mannequin framing all failed identically, with the exact same invisible-stool silhouette every time. This reads as a strong learned association (catalog apparel photography often shows seated fit shots) that prose alone could not override.
fix: NegPip (the one sanctioned negative edit point for mm_image_v1) fixed it on the first attempt after prose failed 7 times: negpip='(sitting:-1.5), (seated:-1.4), (chair:-1.3), (stool:-1.3), (bent knees:-1.0), (crouching:-1.0)'. Standing rule: when a positive-phrased pose/state instruction fails repeatedly (3+ seeds, different phrasing strategies) on mm_image_v1, reach for NegPip rather than continuing to iterate prose -- it suppresses a learned visual bias directly in image space where text conditioning cannot.

finding: mm_chain_v1 (lip-synced performance to a real track) had never been run end to end before this session -- routing.md called it 'not proven' since inception. First real attempt surfaced two genuine bugs: (1) MiniMaxH3ChainAssemble refuses when its mux audio input is a different waveform identity than what H3 Chain Loop Start consumed for conditioning ('received a different source waveform'); (2) landed.py's mm_chain output-path guess (output/h3_chain/<run_name>/final.mp4) was wrong in two ways -- plural 'h3_chains' and a 'final/' subfolder the assemble step actually writes to (output/h3_chains/<run_name>/final/final.mp4) -- so every prior chain job would have silently reported 'completed with no output files' even on success.
fix: (1) Since assemble.py's own audio handling discards each landed clip's baked-in audio when identity.AUDIO.master is set (goose's case) and mixes the ONE external master track over the whole final cut regardless, feeding the chain's internal mux_audio the SAME file as cond_audio is correct, not a workaround -- the chain's own audio output is never actually used downstream. (2) landed.py's output_files() fixed to the confirmed real path. Proof clip (209f, MC rapping the actual opening line, real vocal stem conditioning) landed clean: correct frame count, audio present, visible mouth-shape variation across the filmstrip.
